Jailed HK activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty to foreign collusion | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Prominent Hong Kong pro-democracy campaigner Joshua Wong has pleaded guilty to collusion with foreign entities, a charge that carries a maximum sentence of life in prison under Beijing's sweeping National Security Law (NSL).
 
The 29-year-old, who has become the poster child for political activism in Hong Kong, is already serving a sentence of four years and eight months after being convicted of subversion – another NSL violation – in late 2024.
 
The court said Wong would be sentenced at a later date. His earlier jail term is due to end early next year.
 
Wong was at the forefront of the Umbrella Movement in 2014 and massive pro-democracy protests in 2019.
 
The latest charge accuses Wong of conspiring with other campaigners, including exiled activist Nathan Law, to ask foreign countries and entities outside China to impose sanctions or blockades against Beijing.

119 people rescued in Nepal as death toll passes 1,000 with 4,000 missing | BBC News
recentItems.description:
119 more people have been rescued in Nepal following the deadly flash floods, according to the country’s armed forces.

It comes nearly a week after the disaster that hit both Nepal and neighbouring Tibet. The number of people known to have died in the disaster has passed 1,000, with more than 3,900 missing.

More than 600 of those missing are workers who are believed to be trapped in a vast network of mud-filled tunnels at hydropower sites along the Trishuli River.

The rescue operation is being led by an international team and Nepalese military personnel, with experts from India, Korea and Australia also involved.

Jane Hill presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Azadeh Moshiri in Nepal.

Pakistan deports millions of Afghan refugees, and Norway's king takes throne | Global News Podcast
recentItems.description:
The BBC’s chief international correspondent Lyse Doucet reports from the Pakistani border, as refugees are sent back to Afghanistan. Six million Afghan nationals – some of whom have never set foot in their ancestral homeland – have been deported by Pakistan and Iran since 2023. They now face an uncertain future under the Taliban government.

US attacks Iran after oil tankers struck in Strait of Hormuz | BBC News
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump said the United States has carried out a new wave of strikes on Iran, in response to attempted Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and against US service personnel stationed in the Middle East.
 
Ahead of the strikes, the Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had said his country was willing to return to the conditions of the Memorandum of Understanding signed between the US and Iran in June.
 
Those comments came as Pezeshkian met with Russia's President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan. The Iranian president told his Russian counterpart that together their two countries could resist what he called “US unilateralism”.
